# Lowwin Telegram compatibility package

This private, readable Mini App compatibility port derives from `better-auth-telegram@2.0.1`'s `miniapp-endpoints.ts`, `verify.ts`, `schema.ts`, `config-endpoint.ts`, constants and relevant types. Upstream: https://github.com/vcode-sh/better-auth-telegram. The exact published ESM artifact used to identify those functions has SHA256 `08c77369a9ab8a26d05e2ae870bc954aef432e1994976aae301e7ee5e443879e`. The MIT license and copyright are retained verbatim in LICENSE. Generated bundles, source maps, client/widget code, OIDC code and bundled JOSE dependencies are not shipped.

The upstream package declares Better Auth <1.7.0. Lowwin tests this fork against exact patched Better Auth 1.7.14, without an npm peer override or an older vulnerable copy. The enabled Mini App paths use public adapter, endpoint, session-cookie and rate-limit APIs that remain available in 1.7.14. Better Auth 1.7.3 reverted the transient issuer-schema change, so existing providerId/accountId identities are preserved without a core-table migration.

The port exposes only `telegram`, preserves the Mini App endpoint, HMAC, adapter, session-cookie and per-endpoint rate-limit behavior, and rejects Login Widget, OIDC and Mini App signature-validation bypass. It caps authentication age at the application's existing 300 seconds. Those unneeded flows are outside this fork's compatibility contract. Lowwin's outer handler continues to enforce raw signature/freshness, origin, body limits, identity and contact binding, referral/ledger transaction boundaries and session-token redaction. No account is linked by email, and the application's linking option remains disabled.

Validation lives in tests/auth-dependency-security.test.ts plus the existing auth, Telegram, own-contact, session, role and payment suites. It includes password hashes and signed session cookies generated by the pre-upgrade 1.6.33 library, existing Telegram account identity, and concurrent database rate limiting. The application's gated local-development provisioner now supplies the new 1.7 `createUser` source argument. Future Better Auth upgrades require review and these regressions before changing the exact peer. Replace this port with a maintained compatible upstream package when available. Do not enable the unsupported paths by removing the guard.
